title: OAB Knowledge Unit
description: The YAML frontmatter contract for a knowledge unit in knowledge/. One file, one concept. The body follows a fixed heading skeleton so an agent can locate a section without reading the whole file.

id.description: Stable, repo-unique identifier. Never change it; record former ids in `aliases` instead, because other units link by id.

description.description: One sentence. Used in generated indexes and by an agent deciding whether to read the unit, so it must state what the concept is, not why it is interesting.

category.description: Must match the directory the file lives in. Categories beyond the six M1 domains are reserved for M2.

maturity.description: Trust signal. Agents prefer `stable` and must flag `draft` content as provisional. `draft` is a legitimate landing state for a good but unreviewed contribution.

confidence.description: How settled the industry is on this. `low` means genuine disagreement exists — the unit must record the disagreement rather than pick a side silently.

applies_at_stage.description: Maturity stages where this concept is relevant. THE PRIMARY OVERENGINEERING GUARD: retrieval filters on this, so a stage-4 concept cannot surface in a stage-1 design. Set it deliberately — listing every stage is almost always wrong unless the concept is genuinely scale-independent, like tested backups or timeouts.

prerequisites.description: Concepts required to understand this one. Must not form a cycle.

related.description: Peer concepts. Cross-domain edges are the most valuable ones in the graph: they encode what a specialist knows and a generalist misses.

aliases.description: Former ids, so links from other units keep resolving after a rename.

trade_offs.description: Structured, not prose. An entry with no costs means the concept has not been understood.

when_worth_it.description: Quantified where possible. This is the field that turns knowledge into a decision.

symptom.description: What an operator observes, not what happens internally.

detection.description: The specific signal or metric that reveals it. 'Monitoring' is not detection.

triggers.description: Measurable conditions that make this concept relevant. Generates the trigger library, so these must be observable metrics rather than narrative conditions.

window.description: A sustained period. Instantaneous triggers fire on spikes and get ignored.

action.description: A next step such as 're-run capacity analysis', not a predetermined solution.

complexity_cost.description: Operational burden if adopted, in complexity points. 0 means free (a technique, not a component). Feeds the complexity budget. See frameworks/complexity-budget/weights.yaml.

references.description: At least one attributable source. Summarise concepts in original prose; verbatim copyrighted text is prohibited.

last_reviewed.description: Staleness signal. CI warns beyond 18 months, because knowledge with concrete figures rots.
